# coordinator: «we should do what the standard supports, and avoid
# over-refusal if we can. That's what (b) means right?»; design
# docs/2026-09-05_e13-b-design.md). The §2 gc probe family as rows: a
# spec-UNSEQUENCED panicky non-call operand LEFT of a sibling ordered
# event. The machine offers BOTH orders (`ChoiceSite.unseqPanic`, bound
# 2 exactly when the operand panics at its lexical position): RAISE =
# the operand's panic before the sibling event, DEFER = the sibling
# event first (the pre-change machine's only member). gc's member is
# EARLY (RAISE) for type assertions, slice expressions and interface
# every gc draw lies in the certified set. The witness `wit` PRINTS, so
# the output half of the observation records which sibling events
# completed before the panic — the §7 item-5 'which panic wins and what
# ran before it' observable. expected_reason on a panic row is the
# substring gc's draws carry (the pre-filter is over gc samples only; if
# the oracle ever drew the other member the row would fail loudly).
# Strict controls: forced-arg-only (F2, a singleton), assert-right-call
# (design §6 residual 1: an operand RIGHT of the event realizes only the
# lexical order — gc agrees), assert-left-min-inline (an inline min: both
# operands in the residual, left to right), slice-left-len-call (design
# §6: the slice expression is the hoisted len's OWN operand, evaluated at
# len's position — the lexical member only; gc agrees).
